```text
10	#
11	# Why this script exists:
12	#   Global skills (`~/.agents/skills/`) are restored by

14	#   from the merged ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json. That handles the "every
15	#   machine" case.
16	#
17	#   Project skills (`./.agents/skills/` inside this repo) are different: they
18	#   only make sense when an agent is launched from the repo working tree to
19	#   edit the repo itself. Without this script, after a fresh `chezmoi init`
20	#   on a new machine you'd have to remember to manually run
21	#   `just bootstrap-skills` before agents could see project-scope skills.
22	#
23	# Trigger: changes to the project lock file's content.
24	#   skills-lock.json: {{ if (joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir "skills-lock.json" | stat) }}{{ include (joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir "skills-lock.json") | sha256sum }}{{ else }}absent{{ end }}
25	#
26	# Idempotent: `npx skills experimental_install` skips skills already present
27	# at ./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.
28	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md (Project scope section).
29	
30	set -eu
31	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
32	
33	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
34	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
35	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	
37	SOURCE_DIR={{ .chezmoi.sourceDir | quote }}
38	LOCK="$SOURCE_DIR/skills-lock.json"
39	
40	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
41	  # Not editing the chezmoi repo from this machine — nothing to do.
42	  # (Most consumer machines clone via `chezmoi init` into ~/.local/share/chezmoi
43	  # which IS the repo, so they'll still hit the path below; this branch only
44	  # triggers for unusual setups where source dir ≠ repo root.)
45	  exit 0
46	fi
47	
48	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
49	  warn "npx not installed; cannot bootstrap project skills — skipping."

51	  exit 0
52	fi
53	
54	cd "$SOURCE_DIR"
55	
56	# Fast-path check: if every skill named in the lock already has a SKILL.md,
57	# don't even invoke npx (saves ~3-5s per `chezmoi apply`).
58	if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
59	  all_present=true
60	  while IFS= read -r name; do
61	    [ -z "$name" ] && continue
62	    if [ ! -f "./.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
63	      all_present=false
64	      break
65	    fi
66	  done < <(jq -r '.skills | keys[]' "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null)

68	  if [ "$all_present" = "true" ]; then

70	    exit 0
71	  fi
72	fi
73	
74	info "Bootstrapping project-scope agent skills from $LOCK"
75	if npx -y skills@latest experimental_install >/dev/null 2>&1; then
76	  success "Project agent skills sync complete."
77	else
```

```text
1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Restore globally-installed agent skills from ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json.
3	#
4	# The skills CLI (vercel-labs/skills) does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
5	# from a lock file (issues #283 / #549), so we hand-roll restore here:
6	#   1. The lock file itself is chezmoi-managed via dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl
7	#      (merger that preserves per-machine state).
8	#   2. This script reads the merged lock and, for any entry whose
9	#      ~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is missing, runs
10	#      `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` to (re)install it.
11	#
12	# Trigger: changes to the merger script's $managed block (the source-of-truth list).
13	#   merger: {{ include "dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
14	#
15	# Idempotent: a re-run with no missing skills is a no-op.
16	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
17	
18	set -eu
19	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
20	
21	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
22	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
23	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
24	
25	LOCK="$HOME/.agents/.skill-lock.json"
26	
27	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
28	  warn "Global lock file not found at $LOCK — skipping (chezmoi apply should create it)."
29	  exit 0
30	fi
31	
32	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
33	  warn "jq not installed; cannot parse $LOCK — skipping. Run \`chezmoi apply\` again after the base ansible role finishes."
34	  exit 0
35	fi
36	
37	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
38	  warn "npx not installed; cannot restore global skills — skipping."
39	  exit 0
40	fi
41	
42	# Collect names of skills declared in the lock that are missing on disk.
43	missing=()
44	while IFS=$'\t' read -r name source; do
45	  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
46	  if [ ! -f "$HOME/.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
47	    missing+=("$name"$'\t'"$source")
48	  fi
49	done < <(jq -r '.skills | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value.source)"' "$LOCK")
50	
51	if [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
52	  info "All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install."
53	  exit 0
54	fi
55	
56	info "Restoring ${#missing[@]} missing global skill(s) via \`npx skills add ... -g\`"
57	for entry in "${missing[@]}"; do
58	  name="${entry%%$'\t'*}"
59	  source="${entry##*$'\t'}"
60	  info "  → $name (from $source)"
61	  # Note: -s <name> filters to one skill within multi-skill repos.
62	  # No -a flag → npx prompts auto-detect agents from $HOME/.<agent>/ presence.
63	  if npx -y skills@latest add "$source" -s "$name" -g -y >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    success "    installed $name"
65	  else
66	    warn "    failed to install $name (continuing)"
67	  fi
68	done
69	
70	success "Global agent skills sync complete."
```

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: maintain ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json (the *global*
3	# skills-cli lock file at https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
4	#
5	# Why managed?  The skills CLI does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
6	# from a lock file (see vercel-labs/skills #283 / #549). So to keep "must-have"
7	# global agent skills consistent across machines we treat the lock file as the
8	# single source of truth: this script merges the *managed set* below into
9	# whatever the live lock contains, then `run_onchange_after_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`
10	# reinstalls any entries whose `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is missing.
11	#
12	# Why merge instead of overwrite?  Locally added skills (`npx skills add … -g`
13	# without `-y` followed by chezmoi re-add) should NOT be wiped on every
14	# `chezmoi apply`.  We only enforce *presence* of the managed entries; any
15	# extra `skills.<name>` entries in the live file are preserved verbatim,
16	# along with `dismissed` flags and `lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state.
17	#
18	# To add a new must-have global skill: append an object to $managed.skills below,
19	# matching the schema chezmoi found when first running `npx skills add … -g`
20	# (run `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` after a fresh install for reference).
21	#
22	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role).
23	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
24	set -eu
25	
26	managed=$(cat <<'JSON'
27	{
28	  "version": 3,
29	  "skills": {
30	    "project-knowledge-harness": {
31	      "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills",
32	      "sourceType": "github",
33	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills.git",
34	      "skillPath": "skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md"
35	    },
36	    "find-skills": {
37	      "source": "vercel-labs/skills",
38	      "sourceType": "github",
39	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills.git",
40	      "skillPath": "skills/find-skills/SKILL.md"
41	    }
42	  }
43	}
44	JSON
45	)
46	
47	base=$(cat)
48	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{"version":3,"skills":{}}'
49	
50	# Merge strategy:
51	#   - .version: take the higher of the two (forward-compatible with skills CLI bumps)
52	#   - .skills: for every name in $managed.skills, ensure presence; if the live file
53	#     already has it, keep its installedAt/updatedAt/skillFolderHash (they encode
54	#     real install state) but overwrite source/sourceUrl/skillPath from $managed
55	#     (those are the contract we enforce).
56	#   - .skills.<name> entries NOT in $managed.skills are preserved as-is.
57	#   - .dismissed and .lastSelectedAgents: preserve from live (per-machine state).
58	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson managed "$managed" '
59	  . as $base
60	  | ($base.skills // {}) as $live_skills
61	  | ($managed.skills // {}) as $managed_skills
62	  | {
63	      version: ([($base.version // 0), ($managed.version // 0)] | max),
64	      skills: (
65	        $live_skills
66	        + (
67	            $managed_skills
68	            | to_entries
69	            | map({
70	                key: .key,
71	                value: (
72	                  ($live_skills[.key] // {})
73	                  + (.value | with_entries(select(.key | IN("source","sourceType","sourceUrl","skillPath"))))
74	                )
75	              })
76	            | from_entries
77	          )
78	      )
79	    }
80	    + (if ($base.dismissed // null) != null         then {dismissed:         $base.dismissed}         else {} end)
81	    + (if ($base.lastSelectedAgents // null) != null then {lastSelectedAgents: $base.lastSelectedAgents} else {} end)
82	'
83
```

```text
170	| Command | What it does |
171	|---|---|
172	| `npx skills experimental_install` | Restores **project** lock (`./skills-lock.json`) only |
173	| `npx skills experimental_install -g` | `-g` is **silently ignored**, still project-only ([#283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283), [#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)) |
174	| `npx skills update -g` | Updates already-installed global skills; does **not** backfill missing entries from the lock |
175	| `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` | The only working "restore one missing global skill" idiom — what `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` loops over |
176	
177	### CLI flag gotchas
178	
179	- **Repo shorthand requires `/skills` suffix when skills live under `skills/`**.
180	  `npx skills add owner/repo` looks at `.agents/skills/` in that repo;
181	  `npx skills add owner/repo/skills` looks at `skills/`. Most third-party skill
182	  repos use the latter layout.
183	- **`-a` does NOT take comma-separated values**. Repeat the flag:
184	  `-a claude-code -a opencode -a cursor`.
185	- **Agent names are normalised** (`claude-code` not `claude`,
186	  `gemini-cli` not `gemini`, `copilot` not `github-copilot`). Run
187	  `npx skills add --list` (or trigger the validation error) to see the
188	  canonical list.
189	
190	### Per-agent env var overrides
191	
192	Agents that respect a custom config dir change where the symlink/skill is
193	read from:
194	
195	| Env var | Default | Effect |
196	|---|---|---|
197	| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `~/.claude` | Skills CLI writes symlinks here instead |
198	| `CODEX_HOME` | `~/.codex` | Codex picks up skills from here (Codex is universal, so the global install relies on `~/.agents/skills/` regardless) |
199	| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | `~/.config` | Affects Cursor/OpenCode/Gemini-CLI lookup paths |
200	
201	If you set any of these and re-run `npx skills add -g`, the CLI writes to the
202	new location; chezmoi's lock-file management still uses
203	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (the lock is location-independent).
204	
205	## Anti-patterns
206	
207	- **Don't put skill source files (`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
208	  templates, etc.) in chezmoi source.** They're owned by the npx skills CLI;
209	  chezmoi managing them creates a constant fight with the CLI's
210	  `skillFolderHash`. Only the **lock file** is chezmoi-managed.
211	- **Don't run `chezmoi re-add ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`** to capture local
212	  changes. Edit the merger's `$managed` block instead — that's the
213	  source-of-truth list. `re-add` would freeze a snapshot of one machine's
214	  state into the source, defeating the merger's per-machine preservation.
215	- **Don't commit `./.agents/skills/`**. They're skill source clones that the
216	  npx CLI rewrites on every `update`; tracking them creates noisy diffs and
217	  accidental conflicts with upstream skill updates.
218	- **Don't add `-g` to `bootstrap-skills`**. That recipe is project-scope by
219	  design; global is owned by `chezmoi apply`.
220	
221	## References
222	
223	- Live `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — merger source of truth
224	- Live `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — restore loop
225	- [`vercel-labs/skills` README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) — CLI docs
226	- [Issue #283 — `skills install -g`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283)
227	- [Issue #549 — global lock restore](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)
228	- [`docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`](agent-overlays.md) — sibling pattern for
229	  Claude/Cursor/OpenCode `settings.json` overlays (also `modify_` based)
230
```

```text
48	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{"version":3,"skills":{}}'
49	
50	# Merge strategy:
51	#   - .version: take the higher of the two (forward-compatible with skills CLI bumps)
52	#   - .skills: for every name in $managed.skills, ensure presence; if the live file
53	#     already has it, keep its installedAt/updatedAt/skillFolderHash (they encode
54	#     real install state) but overwrite source/sourceUrl/skillPath from $managed
55	#     (those are the contract we enforce).
56	#   - .skills.<name> entries NOT in $managed.skills are preserved as-is.
57	#   - .dismissed and .lastSelectedAgents: preserve from live (per-machine state).
58	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson managed "$managed" '
59	  . as $base
60	  | ($base.skills // {}) as $live_skills
61	  | ($managed.skills // {}) as $managed_skills
62	  | {
63	      version: ([($base.version // 0), ($managed.version // 0)] | max),
64	      skills: (
65	        $live_skills
66	        + (
67	            $managed_skills
68	            | to_entries
69	            | map({
70	                key: .key,
71	                value: (
72	                  ($live_skills[.key] // {})
73	                  + (.value | with_entries(select(.key | IN("source","sourceType","sourceUrl","skillPath"))))
74	                )
75	              })
76	            | from_entries
77	          )
78	      )
79	    }
80	    + (if ($base.dismissed // null) != null         then {dismissed:         $base.dismissed}         else {} end)
81	    + (if ($base.lastSelectedAgents // null) != null then {lastSelectedAgents: $base.lastSelectedAgents} else {} end)
82	'
```

```text
1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Restore globally-installed agent skills from ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json.
3	#
4	# The skills CLI (vercel-labs/skills) does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
5	# from a lock file (issues #283 / #549), so we hand-roll restore here:
6	#   1. The lock file itself is chezmoi-managed via dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl
7	#      (merger that preserves per-machine state).
8	#   2. This script reads the merged lock and, for any entry whose
9	#      ~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is missing, runs
10	#      `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` to (re)install it.
11	#
12	# Trigger: changes to the merger script's $managed block (the source-of-truth list).
13	#   merger: {{ include "dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
14	#
15	# Idempotent: a re-run with no missing skills is a no-op.
16	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
17	
18	set -eu
19	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
20	
21	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
22	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
23	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
24	
25	LOCK="$HOME/.agents/.skill-lock.json"
26	
27	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
28	  warn "Global lock file not found at $LOCK — skipping (chezmoi apply should create it)."
29	  exit 0
30	fi
31	
32	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
33	  warn "jq not installed; cannot parse $LOCK — skipping. Run \`chezmoi apply\` again after the base ansible role finishes."
34	  exit 0
35	fi
36	
37	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
38	  warn "npx not installed; cannot restore global skills — skipping."
39	  exit 0
40	fi
41	
42	# Collect names of skills declared in the lock that are missing on disk.
43	missing=()
44	while IFS=$'\t' read -r name source; do
45	  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
46	  if [ ! -f "$HOME/.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
47	    missing+=("$name"$'\t'"$source")
48	  fi
49	done < <(jq -r '.skills | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value.source)"' "$LOCK")
50	
51	if [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
52	  info "All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install."
53	  exit 0
54	fi
55	
56	info "Restoring ${#missing[@]} missing global skill(s) via \`npx skills add ... -g\`"
57	for entry in "${missing[@]}"; do
58	  name="${entry%%$'\t'*}"
59	  source="${entry##*$'\t'}"
60	  info "  → $name (from $source)"
61	  # Note: -s <name> filters to one skill within multi-skill repos.
62	  # No -a flag → npx prompts auto-detect agents from $HOME/.<agent>/ presence.
63	  if npx -y skills@latest add "$source" -s "$name" -g -y >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    success "    installed $name"
65	  else
66	    warn "    failed to install $name (continuing)"
67	  fi
68	done
69	
70	success "Global agent skills sync complete."
71
```

```text
7	# Scope encoded by directory: lives under `.chezmoiscripts/repo/` because it
8	# only fires when the source dir IS this repo. Global counterparts live under
9	# `.chezmoiscripts/global/`. See docs/this_repo/chezmoiscripts-layout.md.
10	#
11	# Why this script exists:
12	#   Global skills (`~/.agents/skills/`) are restored by
13	#   .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl
14	#   from the merged ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json. That handles the "every
15	#   machine" case.
16	#
17	#   Project skills (`./.agents/skills/` inside this repo) are different: they
18	#   only make sense when an agent is launched from the repo working tree to
19	#   edit the repo itself. Without this script, after a fresh `chezmoi init`
20	#   on a new machine you'd have to remember to manually run
21	#   `just bootstrap-skills` before agents could see project-scope skills.
22	#
23	# Trigger: changes to the project lock file's content.
24	#   skills-lock.json: {{ if (joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir "skills-lock.json" | stat) }}{{ include (joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir "skills-lock.json") | sha256sum }}{{ else }}absent{{ end }}
25	#
26	# Idempotent: `npx skills experimental_install` skips skills already present
27	# at ./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.
28	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md (Project scope section).
29	
30	set -eu
31	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
32	
33	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
34	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
35	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	
37	SOURCE_DIR={{ .chezmoi.sourceDir | quote }}
38	LOCK="$SOURCE_DIR/skills-lock.json"
39	
40	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
41	  # Not editing the chezmoi repo from this machine — nothing to do.
42	  # (Most consumer machines clone via `chezmoi init` into ~/.local/share/chezmoi
43	  # which IS the repo, so they'll still hit the path below; this branch only
44	  # triggers for unusual setups where source dir ≠ repo root.)
45	  exit 0
46	fi
47	
48	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
49	  warn "npx not installed; cannot bootstrap project skills — skipping."
50	  warn "Run \`just bootstrap-skills\` later from $SOURCE_DIR after Node is available."
51	  exit 0
52	fi
53	
54	cd "$SOURCE_DIR"
55	
56	# Fast-path check: if every skill named in the lock already has a SKILL.md,
57	# don't even invoke npx (saves ~3-5s per `chezmoi apply`).
58	if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
59	  all_present=true
60	  while IFS= read -r name; do
61	    [ -z "$name" ] && continue
62	    if [ ! -f "./.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
63	      all_present=false
64	      break
65	    fi
66	  done < <(jq -r '.skills | keys[]' "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null)
67	
68	  if [ "$all_present" = "true" ]; then
69	    info "All project-scope agent skills present at ./.agents/skills/; nothing to install."
70	    exit 0
71	  fi
72	fi
73	
74	info "Bootstrapping project-scope agent skills from $LOCK"
75	if npx -y skills@latest experimental_install >/dev/null 2>&1; then
76	  success "Project agent skills sync complete."
77	else
78	  warn "npx skills experimental_install failed; run \`just bootstrap-skills\` manually to retry."
79	  exit 0  # don't fail the whole `chezmoi apply` over a non-critical bootstrap
80	fi
81
```

```text
177	### CLI flag gotchas
178	
179	- **Repo shorthand requires `/skills` suffix when skills live under `skills/`**.

181	  `npx skills add owner/repo/skills` looks at `skills/`. Most third-party skill
182	  repos use the latter layout.
183	- **`-a` does NOT take comma-separated values**. Repeat the flag:

185	- **Agent names are normalised** (`claude-code` not `claude`,
```

# Fix project-scope agent skill installation source

## Context

`just bootstrap-skills` (and the matching `chezmoi apply` run-script) fail to restore the three project-scope agent skills: `agent-history-hygiene`, `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`, `project-knowledge-harness`. The upstream clone succeeds but the installer reports:

\```
No matching skills found for: agent-history-hygiene, mkdocs-site-bootstrap, project-knowledge-harness
Available skills:
  - find-skills
  - skill-creator
\```

Root cause: the `source` field in our two lock files is `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` without the `/skills` suffix. Per [`docs/tools/agent-skills.md:179-182`](../../docs/tools/agent-skills.md):

> `npx skills add owner/repo` looks at `.agents/skills/` in that repo; `npx skills add owner/repo/skills` looks at `skills/`.

Upstream [`daviddwlee84/agent-skills`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills) keeps our three skills under `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/`, while its `.agents/skills/` only contains `find-skills` + `skill-creator` — which is exactly what the installer is listing as "available". The correct source to pass is `daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.

Intended outcome: `chezmoi apply` on a fresh machine restores all 3 project-scope skills silently, and `just bootstrap-skills` succeeds.

## Files to change

### 1. `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/skills-lock.json`

Hand-maintained project lock consumed by `npx skills experimental_install`. Update three `source` fields:

- Line 5 (`agent-history-hygiene`): `"daviddwlee84/agent-skills"` → `"daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"`
- Line 10 (`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`): same
- Line 15 (`project-knowledge-harness`): same

Leave `computedHash` values untouched — the hash is over skill folder contents, not the source URL, so if the upstream commit is unchanged it will still verify. If `npx skills experimental_install` later complains about hash mismatch, regenerate by re-running `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills -s <name> -y` for each skill (that rewrites `skills-lock.json` with fresh hashes).

chezmoi `modify_` merger that maintains `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (the global skills-cli lock). The `$managed` JSON literal (line 26-45) hard-codes one entry from `daviddwlee84/agent-skills`:

- Line 31 (`project-knowledge-harness`): `"source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills"` → `"source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"`

Do NOT touch the `find-skills` entry on line 37 (`"source": "vercel-labs/skills"`). It's a different upstream repo, currently installs successfully, and the user did not report it broken — leave it as-is to avoid scope creep.

The downstream script `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` reads `.source` verbatim and passes it to `npx skills@latest add "$source" -s "$name" -g -y` at line 63, so fixing the merger is sufficient — no code change needed in the install script.

```text
#!/bin/sh
# chezmoi modify_ script: maintain ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json (the *global*
# skills-cli lock file at https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
#
# Why managed?  The skills CLI does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
# from a lock file (see vercel-labs/skills #283 / #549). So to keep "must-have"
# global agent skills consistent across machines we treat the lock file as the
# single source of truth: this script merges the *managed set* below into
# whatever the live lock contains, then `run_onchange_after_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`
# reinstalls any entries whose `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is missing.
#
# Why merge instead of overwrite?  Locally added skills (`npx skills add … -g`
# without `-y` followed by chezmoi re-add) should NOT be wiped on every
# `chezmoi apply`.  We only enforce *presence* of the managed entries; any
# extra `skills.<name>` entries in the live file are preserved verbatim,
# along with `dismissed` flags and `lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state.
#
# To add a new must-have global skill: append an object to $managed.skills below,
# matching the schema chezmoi found when first running `npx skills add … -g`
# (run `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` after a fresh install for reference).
#
# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role).
# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
set -eu

managed=$(cat <<'JSON'
{
  "version": 3,
  "skills": {
    "project-knowledge-harness": {
      "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills",
      "sourceType": "github",
      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills.git",
      "skillPath": "skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md"
    },
    "find-skills": {
      "source": "vercel-labs/skills",
      "sourceType": "github",
      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills.git",
      "skillPath": "skills/find-skills/SKILL.md"
    }
  }
}
JSON
)

base=$(cat)
[ -z "$base" ] && base='{"version":3,"skills":{}}'

# Merge strategy:
#   - .version: take the higher of the two (forward-compatible with skills CLI bumps)
#   - .skills: for every name in $managed.skills, ensure presence; if the live file
#     already has it, keep its installedAt/updatedAt/skillFolderHash (they encode
#     real install state) but overwrite source/sourceUrl/skillPath from $managed
#     (those are the contract we enforce).
#   - .skills.<name> entries NOT in $managed.skills are preserved as-is.
#   - .dismissed and .lastSelectedAgents: preserve from live (per-machine state).
printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson managed "$managed" '
  . as $base
  | ($base.skills // {}) as $live_skills
```
</details></tool-use>

Fix landed and verified end-to-end. Summary:

- **`skills-lock.json`** (3 entries) and **`dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`** (1 entry for `project-knowledge-harness`): appended the required `/skills` suffix so `npx skills` resolves against upstream's `skills/local` + `skills/vendor` trees instead of its `.agents/skills/` (which only holds `find-skills` + `skill-creator`).

One quirk worth flagging: the `npx skills experimental_install` CLI normalizes the `source` field when it rewrites the lock (strips the `/skills` suffix back off). That didn't affect correctness here — once skills are on disk, the fast-path short-circuits before npx runs — but on a fresh machine the first-install rewrite will create a local drift vs. the repo-committed lock.
```text
{"body":"## Description\n\nWhen `skills-lock.json` contains an explicit SSH URL as `source` (e.g. `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`), running `experimental_install` successfully clones via SSH — but then overwrites the lock file, replacing the SSH URL with the `owner/repo` shorthand. On the next `experimental_install`, the shorthand is resolved to HTTPS, breaking restore for private repos.\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Manually set `source` to an SSH URL in `skills-lock.json`:\n```json\n   {\n     \"create-service-specific-skill\": {\n       \"source\": \"git@github.com:myorg/private-repo.git\",\n       \"sourceType\": \"git\"\n     }\n   }\n```\n2. Run `bunx skills experimental_install` — clone succeeds via SSH ✓\n3. Inspect `skills-lock.json` — `source` is now `\"myorg/private-repo\"` (SSH URL overwritten)\n4. Run `bunx skills experimental_install` again — fails with HTTPS auth error\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\n`experimental_install` should preserve the original `source` value from `skills-lock.json` rather than normalizing it. If the user specified an SSH URL, it should remain as-is after install.\n\n## Actual Behavior\n\nAfter a successful install, `add.ts:1521` writes back to the lock file using `normalizedSource` (the result of `getOwnerRepo(parsed)`), which strips the SSH URL down to `owner/repo` shorthand. On the next run, `parseSource()` treats that shorthand as a GitHub shorthand and builds an HTTPS URL.\n\n## Root Cause\n\nIn `src/add.ts:1521`:\n```ts\nsource: normalizedSource || parsed.url,\n```\n`normalizedSource` is always populated for SSH GitHub URLs (extracts `owner/repo`), so `parsed.url` (the original SSH URL) is never preserved.\n\n## Workaround\n\nRe-set the SSH URL in `skills-lock.json` after every `skills add` or `experimental_install`, or configure git globally:\n```bash\ngit config --global url.\"git@github.com:\".insteadOf \"https://github.com/\"\n```","number":567,"state":"closed","title":"[Bug]: experimental_install overwrites SSH source URL in skills-lock.json with HTTPS shorthand"}
```

```text
{"body":"### Problem\n\nWhen using the shorthand syntax `npx skills add owner/repo/\u003csubpath\u003e`, the CLI currently only looks for skills at `\u003crepo\u003e/\u003csubpath\u003e`. If that exact path doesn't exist, it immediately fails with \"No skills found\" — even if the skill actually lives at `\u003crepo\u003e/skills/\u003csubpath\u003e`.\n\nThis is a real friction point because placing skills inside a `skills/` subdirectory **is itself an established community convention** — not just a user preference. Both official repos follow this layout:\n- [`anthropics/skills`](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) — skills are under `skills/`\n- [`vercel-labs/skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) — skills are under `skills/`\n\nBecause these authoritative repos set the pattern, when I went to install from my own repo (`owner/skills/ui-design`), my instinct was that `ui-design` referred to a skill inside `skills/`, not a directory at the root. The result was a confusing \"No skills found\" error.\n\n### The Awkward Workaround Today\n\nTo make it work with a repo named `skills` that follows the standard `skills/\u003cname\u003e/` layout, you currently have to write:\n\n```bash\n# Ugly double-nesting — skills/skills/ui-design\nnpx skills add owner/skills/skills/ui-design\n```\n\nThis is clearly unintuitive and breaks down exactly when users follow the community-recommended structure.\n\n### Proposed Behavior\n\nWhen `\u003csubpath\u003e` is provided via the shorthand, `discoverSkills` should resolve it with the following fallback order:\n\n1. **Check `\u003crepo\u003e/\u003csubpath\u003e` first** — exact path, current behavior\n2. **Fall back to `\u003crepo\u003e/skills/\u003csubpath\u003e`** — community convention layout\n3. **Fail with \"No skills found\"** only if both are missing\n\n### Implementation\n\nThe change is small and fully backward-compatible — it only affects the case where the direct `subpath` doesn't exist. No changes needed to `source-parser.ts` or `add.ts`.\n\nChange is limited to `discoverSkills` in `src/skills.ts`: add a `pathExists` helper and a fallback path resolution before the main search logic runs.\n\nI'm happy to submit a PR for this if the direction looks good.\n","number":716,"state":"open","title":"feat: support fallback to skills/\u003csubpath\u003e when subpath is not found at repo root"}
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
{"body":"### Problem\n\nCurrently, the CLI supports subpath specification for HTTPS URLs and GitHub shorthand, but not for SSH URLs:\n\n**✅ Works:**\n```bash\nnpx skills add owner/repo/path/to/skills\nnpx skills add https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/path/to/skills\n```\n\n**❌ Doesn't work:**\n```bash\nnpx skills add git@github.com:owner/repo.git\n# No way to specify a subpath within the repository\n```\n\nThis limitation means users who prefer SSH authentication (or are required to use it for private repositories) cannot easily install skills from a subdirectory without cloning the entire repository and manually filtering.\n\n### Who This Affects\n\nThis issue particularly impacts:\n- **Users with private repositories** who must use SSH authentication but want to install skills from specific subdirectories\n- **Teams managing large monorepos** where skills are organized in nested directory structures and cloning the entire repo is inefficient\n- **Organizations with strict security policies** that mandate SSH over HTTPS for all Git operations\n- **Users expecting consistent CLI behavior** across all Git URL formats, who are surprised that SSH URLs lack feature parity with HTTPS URLs\n\n### Proposed Solution\n\nI'd like to suggest one of the following approaches:\n\n### Option 1: Add `--subpath` flag\n```bash\nnpx skills add git@github.com:owner/repo.git --subpath path/to/skills\n```\n\n**Pros:** Clear and explicit, follows existing CLI conventions  \n**Cons:** Requires an additional flag\n\n### Option 2: Use `@` notation for subpath\n```bash\nnpx skills add git@github.com:owner/repo.git@path/to/skills\n\n# With branch specification:\nnpx skills add git@github.com:owner/repo.git@main:path/to/skills\n```\n\n**Pros:** Compact syntax, familiar from npm/yarn package notation  \n**Cons:** Might be confused with branch/ref specification\n\n### Option 3: Use URL fragment syntax\n```bash\nnpx skills add \"git@github.com:owner/repo.git#path/to/skills\"\n\n# With branch:\nnpx skills add \"git@github.com:owner/repo.git#main:path/to/skills\"\n```\n\n**Pros:** Standard URL fragment pattern, shell-safe with quotes  \n**Cons:** Requires quotes to prevent shell interpretation\n\n### Alternatives Considered\n\n### Current Workaround\n\nThe only current option is to use the `--skill` flag to filter after cloning:\n```bash\nnpx skills add git@github.com:owner/repo.git --skill specific-skill\n```\n\nHowever, this still clones the entire repository and doesn't allow path-based filtering before skill discovery.\n\n### Additional Context\n\n### Implementation Notes\n\nThe change would primarily affect `src/source-parser.ts`:\n\n1. Update the fallback git URL handler (lines 187-191) to parse and extract subpath information\n2. Add support for the chosen notation (e.g., split on `@` or `#` for subpath)\n3. Return the subpath in the `ParsedSource` object alongside the git URL\n4. The existing clone and discovery logic should already handle subpaths correctly\n\nExample implementation for Option 1:\n```typescript\n// In parseSource function, before the fallback:\nif (input.includes('@') \u0026\u0026 input.includes(':') \u0026\u0026 !input.startsWith('http')) {\n  // SSH URL format: git@host:owner/repo.git\n  return {\n    type: 'git',\n    url: input,\n    // subpath would come from --subpath flag in AddOptions\n  };\n}\n```\n\n### Use Cases\n\nThis feature would benefit users who:\n- Work with private repositories requiring SSH authentication\n- Manage large monorepos with skills in subdirectories\n- Have organizational policies requiring SSH over HTTPS\n- Want consistent CLI syntax across all Git URL formats\n\n### Related\n\nThis is consistent with how the CLI already handles HTTPS URLs with paths. It would provide feature parity across all supported Git URL formats.\n\n---\n\nWould this change be acceptable? I'm happy to contribute a PR if you agree on which approach would be best.\n","number":172,"state":"open","title":"[Feature]: Support subpath specification for SSH URLs"}
```

```text
{"body":"## Problem\n\nWhen a skill is installed from an SSH URL (`git@github.com:org/repo.git`), the lock file `source` field is overwritten with the `owner/repo` shorthand (via `getOwnerRepo()`). On the next `experimental_install`, `parseSource()` resolves this shorthand to an HTTPS URL, breaking restore for private repos that require SSH authentication.\n\n## Root Cause\n\n`add.ts` unconditionally uses `normalizedSource` (the `owner/repo` extraction) when writing to both global and local lock files:\n```ts\nsource: normalizedSource,        // global lock\nsource: normalizedSource || parsed.url,  // local lock\n```\n\n## Fix\n\nDetect SSH URLs (`git@...`) and preserve them as-is in lock files instead of normalizing:\n```ts\nconst isSSH = parsed.url.startsWith('git@');\nconst lockSource = isSSH ? parsed.url : normalizedSource;\n```\n\nTelemetry still uses `normalizedSource` (the `owner/repo` form) — only the lock file storage is affected.\n\n## Changes\n\n- **`src/add.ts`**: Added `lockSource` variable that preserves SSH URLs; used in both global lock (`addSkillToLock`) and local lock (`addSkillToLocalLock`) writes.\n\nFixes #567","merged":true,"number":588,"state":"closed","title":"fix: preserve SSH source URLs in lock files"}
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
{"body":"### Description\n\nWhen installing a skill discovered via a well-known discovery URL (sourceType: `well-known`) as a project-scoped install, the entry written to the local `skills-lock.json` uses a truncated `source` value (an identifier) instead of the full original URL. This prevents `npx skills update` from reconstructing the original install source, causing updates to fail.\n\nAffected code: `src/add.ts` - `handleWellKnownSkills()` writes `source: sourceIdentifier` into the local lock for project installs.\n\nRoot cause\n- `sourceIdentifier` is an owner/repo-style identifier (or hostname fragment) produced by `wellKnownProvider.getSourceIdentifier(url)` and may omit the full protocol/host/path. The local lock's `source` field is later used verbatim by the update path to rebuild the install source; when it's incomplete the updater cannot parse it.\n\nFix (one line)\n- Write the full parsed URL into the local lock for well-known project installs instead of the identifier. Concretely, change the lock write from:\n\n```\n - source: sourceIdentifier,\n + source: url,\n```\n\nNotes\n- This change affects only project-scoped installs for `sourceType: 'well-known'` and preserves the intended semantics of the `source` field (it must contain the original install URL so updates can be rebuilt).\n- Tests in this repository passed when the change was applied locally.\n\n### Steps to Reproduce\n\nI've created this example to help reproducing the issue: https://github.com/smurf667/well-known-skills-update-issue\n\n1. Start the demo server:\n\n```bash\nnpm run start\n```\n\n2. Add the example skill to your project (uses the discovery endpoint served by the demo):\n\n```bash\nnpx skills add http://localhost:8080/demo-skills\n```\n\n3. Attempt to update the skill (uses the generated `skills-lock.json` file):\n\n```bash\nnpx skills update\n```\n\nWhat to expect\n\n- The demo serves the discovery index at:\n  - http://localhost:8080/demo-skills/.well-known/skills/index.json\n- And the skill markdown at:\n  - http://localhost:8080/demo-skills/.well-known/skills/example-skill/SKILL.md\n\n- `npx skills add http://localhost:8080/demo-skills` should install the skill successfully.\n\n- However, running `npx skills update` fails due an incorrect `source`  value.\n\n### Expected Behavior\n\n`npx skills update` works for skills installed from well-known server sources, like the example server.\n\n### Actual Behavior\n\n`npx skills update` fails.\n\n### Version\n\n1.5.1\n\n### Node.js Version\n\n24.7.0\n\n### Operating System\n\nmacOS\n\n### Logs / Error Output\n\n```shell\nnpx skills update\n│\n◇  Update scope\n│  Project\nChecking for skill updates...\n\nRefreshing 1 project skill(s)...\n\nUpdating example-skill...\n  ✗ Failed to update example-skill\n\nFailed to update 1 skill(s)\n```","number":999,"state":"open","title":"[Bug]: well-known source truncated in `skills-lock.json` prevents updates"}
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
{"body":"Summary\n`npx skills add` writes GitLab source as a short slug (example: `it-operations/marketplace-ops`) into `~/skills-lock.json`.\nAfter that, `npx skills update` fails for those skills on self-hosted GitLab.\nIf `source` is manually changed to the full Git URL (`https://...git`), update works.\n\nEnvironment\n- `skills` CLI version: `1.5.1`\n- OS: macOS\n- GitLab: self-hosted (`gitlab.local.net`)\n- Repo used in repro: `https://gitlab.local.net/it-operations/marketplace-ops.git`\n\nSteps to reproduce\n1. Install a skill from self-hosted GitLab:\n   `npx skills add https://gitlab.local.net/it-operations/marketplace-ops.git --skill aws --agent claude-code -y`\n2. Check lock file (`~/skills-lock.json`).\n3. Run:\n   `npx skills update AWS -p -y`\n\nActual result\n- Update fails:\n  - `Updating AWS...`\n  - `✗ Failed to update AWS`\n\nObserved lock entry after install\n- `source: it-operations/marketplace-ops`\n- `sourceType: git`\n\nControl test (works)\n1. Manually patch `~/skills-lock.json` for AWS:\n   - `source: https://gitlab.local.net/it-operations/marketplace-ops.git`\n   - `sourceType: git`\n2. Run:\n   `npx skills update AWS -p -y`\n3. Result: `✓ Updated AWS`\n\nExpected result\n- `npx skills update` should work for self-hosted GitLab sources installed via `npx skills add` without manual lock-file edits.\n\nSuggestion\nEither:\n1. Preserve full Git URL for self-hosted GitLab in `skills-lock.json`, or\n2. Resolve short GitLab slug correctly for self-hosted hosts during `update`.\n\nImpact\nTeams using private/self-hosted GitLab cannot reliably use `npx skills update` and must manually patch `skills-lock.json`.","number":997,"state":"open","title":"`npx skills update` fails for self-hosted GitLab when source is normalized to short slug"}
```

```text
{"body":"## Summary\n\n`.skill-lock.json` currently has two related correctness problems:\n\n1. harmless-looking metadata writes can be lossy\n2. skills from different sources that share the same visible name collide in the lockfile\n\n## Why this matters\n\nThis makes the lockfile unreliable as a source of truth for global skill ownership.\n\nThe failure modes include:\n- tracked skills disappearing during metadata updates\n- one source overwriting another when both provide the same skill name\n- grouped source views losing entries\n- follow-on commands operating on incomplete or ambiguous lock state\n\n## Current behavior\n\n### 1. Lossy rewrites\n\nOperations like prompt dismissal / agent preference updates rewrite the same global lockfile.\n\nIf the lockfile shape is older or contains fields the reader does not round-trip, those writes can drop tracked state or unknown top-level metadata.\n\n### 2. Same-name collisions\n\nLock entries are keyed by visible skill name, so two different sources that both expose `shared-skill` collide.\n\nThat means:\n- later writes overwrite earlier ones\n- grouping by source loses one side\n- removal/update semantics become ambiguous\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n- metadata-only writes should not drop tracked skill entries or unknown top-level fields\n- skills from different sources should have distinct lockfile identity even if the visible skill name is the same\n- grouping/removal helpers should preserve all tracked variants\n\n## Suggested direction\n\nUse source-aware lock identity and make lockfile reads/writes preserve unknown fields instead of silently normalizing them away.\n","number":606,"state":"open","title":".skill-lock.json rewrites are lossy and same-name skills from different sources collide"}
```
</details></tool-use>

cat > /tmp/skills-issue-body.md <<'EOF'
## Description

When `skills-lock.json` contains a `source` in the form `owner/repo/<subpath>` (e.g. `daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`), `experimental_install` clones and installs successfully, but then rewrites the lock file with the subpath **stripped** (`daviddwlee84/agent-skills`). Subsequent restores from the mutated lock fail, because the CLI now looks for skills under `.agents/skills/` in the repo instead of the originally-specified `skills/` subpath.

This is the same class of bug as #567 / #588 (which preserved SSH URLs), just applied to the `owner/repo/<subpath>` shorthand. The `normalizedSource` code path in `src/add.ts` strips the subpath component on lock write-back.

## Reproduction (self-contained)

Requires `jq` and Node. Copy-paste into a shell:

\```bash
# --- PART 1: demonstrate the write-back strips /skills subpath ---
WORK=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$WORK"

cat > skills-lock.json <<'JSON'
{
  "version": 1,
  "skills": {
    "project-knowledge-harness": {
      "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills",
      "sourceType": "github"
    }
  }
}
JSON

echo "BEFORE: $(jq -r '.skills["project-knowledge-harness"].source' skills-lock.json)"
npx -y skills@latest experimental_install >/dev/null 2>&1
AFTER=$(jq -r '.skills["project-knowledge-harness"].source' skills-lock.json)
echo "AFTER:  $AFTER"
[ "$AFTER" = "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills" ] && echo "PASS (subpath preserved)" || echo "FAIL (subpath stripped)"
\```

**Observed output:**

\```
BEFORE: daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
AFTER:  daviddwlee84/agent-skills
FAIL (subpath stripped)
\```

## Second-order failure (fresh-machine restore is broken)

\```bash
# --- PART 2: the mutated lock now fails to restore on a fresh machine ---
WORK=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$WORK"
cat > skills-lock.json <<'JSON'
{
  "version": 1,
  "skills": {
    "project-knowledge-harness": {
      "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills",
      "sourceType": "github"
    }
  }
}
JSON
npx -y skills@latest experimental_install 2>&1 | tail -6
\```

**Observed output:**

\```
◇  Found 2 skills
│
■  No matching skills found for: project-knowledge-harness
●  Available skills:
│    - find-skills
│    - skill-creator
\```

The upstream repo [`daviddwlee84/agent-skills`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills) stores its skills under `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/`; the `/skills` subpath is load-bearing to reach them. Without it, only the two skills physically resident in `.agents/skills/` (`find-skills`, `skill-creator`) are discovered. (Sibling symlinks at `.agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap` etc. exist but are not followed.)

## Expected behaviour

`experimental_install` should preserve the `<subpath>` component of `owner/repo/<subpath>` in `skills-lock.json` on write-back, so that subsequent runs reach the same install source. This is the analogue of #588's SSH-URL fix applied to the shorthand case.

## Suggested fix

Same shape as the #588 patch. In `src/add.ts` where `lockSource` is computed, branch on whether the parsed source has a subpath and preserve it:

\```ts
const lockSource =
  isSSH                  ? parsed.url
  : parsed.subpath       ? `${normalizedSource}/${parsed.subpath}`
  :                        normalizedSource;
\```

(Pseudocode — actual field name on `parsed` differs.)

## Workaround

1. Re-write `skills-lock.json` after every `skills add` / `experimental_install` to restore the `/<subpath>` suffix, or
2. Symlink every skill into `.agents/skills/` upstream (fragile; breaks if the CLI starts following symlinks inconsistently).

A consumer applying workaround (1) across a chezmoi-managed repo + `run_onchange` script: [daviddwlee84/dotfiles#fix-project-scope-agent-skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles) — specifically `skills-lock.json` + `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` needing manual `/skills` restoration after every install.

## Version / environment

- `skills` CLI: **1.5.1** (installed via `npx -y skills@latest`)
- Node: **v24.13.0**
- OS: Linux 5.15 (Ubuntu 22.04)

## References

- **Consuming dotfiles repo** (bug reporter's context): [daviddwlee84/dotfiles](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles) — chezmoi-managed setup that invokes `npx skills experimental_install` from a `run_onchange_after_*` script on every `chezmoi apply`. The `/skills` suffix workaround lives in [`skills-lock.json`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/skills-lock.json) and [`dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl).
- **Upstream skill repo used in the repro**: [daviddwlee84/agent-skills](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills) — skills organised under `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/`, so source must be `owner/repo/skills`, not bare `owner/repo`.
- **Direct precedent**: #567 / PR #588 — same `normalizedSource` code path stripped SSH URLs; the fix preserved them but did not cover subpaths.
- **Adjacent but separate**: #716 / PR #717 — proposes a fallback from `<repo>/<subpath>` → `<repo>/skills/<subpath>` in `discoverSkills` when the exact subpath is missing. That is a search-path convenience; it does **not** address the lock-write-back normalization.
- **Same class of issue** (lossy source normalization in `skills-lock.json`): #606, #997, #999.

Happy to send a PR if the direction in "Suggested fix" looks right.
EOF
wc -l /tmp/skills-issue-body.md

```bash
Adding motivation that I should've included in the original post — the subpath distinction is load-bearing, not a cosmetic preference.

My upstream repo [`daviddwlee84/agent-skills`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills) intentionally separates two categories of skills:

1. **`skills/local/` + `skills/vendor/`** — skills I maintain *for other people* to install (the published surface)
2. **`.agents/skills/`** — skills I install *for myself* to author + maintain the repo (`find-skills`, `skill-creator` — tooling I use while writing the published ones)

When a consumer runs `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`, they should only get category (1). When the CLI strips `/skills` on lock write-back, the next restore resolves to the bare repo shorthand → `.agents/skills/` → category (2), which leaks my authoring tools into the consumer's install and misses the skills they actually wanted.

So this isn't a normalization nit — it collapses the **curation boundary** between "what I publish" and "what I use to author what I publish". I suspect this is also why the larger community repos ([`anthropics/skills`](https://github.com/anthropics/skills), [`vercel-labs/skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)) adopt `skills/` as the publishing root rather than `.agents/skills/`: it leaves `.agents/` free for the maintainer's own workflow without polluting the consumer API.

Tracking on my side:
- [`daviddwlee84/agent-skills` tracker](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/issues) — layout rationale + consumer-facing impact
- [`daviddwlee84/dotfiles` tracker](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/issues) — the workaround in-place until this ships
```

### Impact on consumers of this repo

The intended install command is:

\```bash
npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
\```

The `/skills` suffix is **load-bearing**, not cosmetic. It separates the two categories of skills in this repo:

1. **`skills/local/` + `skills/vendor/`** — skills maintained *for others to install* (the published surface)
2. **`.agents/skills/`** — skills installed *for myself* to author + maintain this repo (`find-skills`, `skill-creator` — tooling used while writing the published ones)

When the CLI strips `/skills` on lock write-back, the next restore resolves to `.agents/skills/` (category 2) and misses the skills consumers actually wanted (category 1). Symptom: `No matching skills found for: ...` followed by `Available skills: find-skills, skill-creator`.

### Workaround (consumer side)

After `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills -y`, manually restore the `/skills` suffix in `skills-lock.json`:

\```json
"<skill-name>": {
  "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"
}
\```

The CLI will strip it again on the next install, but on-disk skills stay valid until then. A downstream chezmoi-managed example: [daviddwlee84/dotfiles → skills-lock.json](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/skills-lock.json).

- vercel-labs/skills#1005 fixed + released
- Verify `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills -y` followed by `npx skills experimental_install` no longer mutates the source field
- Remove workaround notes from README / docs (if any added meanwhile)

Root cause: the CLI was fed `source: "daviddwlee84/agent-skills"` (without `/skills` suffix) and only sees the `.agents/skills/` layout — which holds the upstream maintainer's *authoring* tools, not the published skills. See upstream [daviddwlee84/agent-skills issue](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/issues) for the layout rationale.

### Fix in place (workaround)

Two files hold the `/skills` suffix explicitly and will drift every time the CLI rewrites them on a fresh install:

- [`skills-lock.json`](../blob/main/skills-lock.json) — three project-scope skills, each `source: "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"`
- [`dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`](../blob/main/dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl) — the `project-knowledge-harness` entry in `$managed`

The committed copies stay correct; fresh-machine `chezmoi apply` uses the committed `skills-lock.json` as input, install succeeds, but the CLI's post-install rewrite on the **local** copy strips the suffix. That's harmless because:

1. `.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl` has a fast-path that skips `npx` entirely when every `./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is present.
2. `git status` on the source dir will show `skills-lock.json` as dirty after every `just bootstrap-skills` — expected, revertable with `git checkout skills-lock.json`.

### Close criteria

- vercel-labs/skills#1005 fixed + released
- Re-run `just bootstrap-skills` on a clean tree; verify `skills-lock.json` is **not** modified after the command completes
- Re-run `chezmoi apply`; verify the global install script logs `→ project-knowledge-harness (from daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills)` and the source on disk in `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` keeps the suffix
- Once confirmed, no code change is needed in this repo — both lock files already carry the correct `/skills` suffix. This issue closes as "upstream fixed".

These are NOT local cron jobs — each routine spawns a fully isolated remote session (CCR) in Anthropic's cloud infrastructure, either on a recurring cron schedule or once at a specific time. The agent runs in a sandboxed environment with its own git checkout, tools, and optional MCP connections.

Use the `RemoteTrigger` tool (load it first with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger`; auth is handled in-process — do not use curl):

- `{action: "list"}` — list all routines
- `{action: "get", trigger_id: "..."}` — fetch one routine
- `{action: "create", body: {...}}` — create a routine
- `{action: "update", trigger_id: "...", body: {...}}` — partial update
- `{action: "run", trigger_id: "..."}` — run a routine now

(Note: the API uses `trigger_id` as the parameter name, but the user-facing term is "routine".)

You CANNOT delete routines. If the user asks to delete, direct them to: https://claude.ai/code/routines

## Create body shape

```json
}
```

For a one-time run, replace `"cron_expression": "CRON_EXPR"` with `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"` (RFC3339 UTC, must be in the future). Everything else is identical.

## API Field Reference

### Create Routine — Required Fields
- `name` (string) — A descriptive name
- Exactly ONE of:
  - `cron_expression` (string) — 5-field cron in UTC. **Minimum interval is 1 hour.**
  - `run_once_at` (string) — RFC3339 UTC timestamp. Must be in the future. Fires once, then auto-disables.
- `job_config` (object) — Session configuration (see structure above)

### Create Routine — Optional Fields
- `enabled` (boolean, default: true)
- `mcp_connections` (array) — MCP servers to attach:

### Update Routine — Optional Fields
All fields optional (partial update):
- `name`, `cron_expression`, `run_once_at`, `enabled`, `job_config`
- `mcp_connections` — Replace MCP connections
- `clear_mcp_connections` (boolean) — Remove all MCP connections

### Cron Expression Examples

The user's local timezone is **Asia/Shanghai**. Cron expressions and `run_once_at` timestamps are always in UTC. When the user says a local time, convert it to UTC but confirm with them: "9am Asia/Shanghai = Xam UTC, so the cron would be `0 X * * 1-5`." For one-time runs, the same conversion applies — "run this at 3pm" → `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z"` with their 3pm converted to UTC.

- `0 9 * * 1-5` — Every weekday at 9am **UTC**
- `0 */2 * * *` — Every 2 hours
- `0 0 * * *` — Daily at midnight **UTC**
- `30 14 * * 1` — Every Monday at 2:30pm **UTC**
- `0 8 1 * *` — First of every month at 8am **UTC**

Minimum interval is 1 hour. `*/30 * * * *` will be rejected.

### CREATE a new routine:

1. **Understand the goal** — Ask what they want the remote agent to do. What repo(s)? What task? Remind them that the agent runs remotely — it won't have access to their local machine, local files, or local environment variables.
2. **Craft the prompt** — Help them write an effective agent prompt. Good prompts are:
   - Specific about what to do and what success looks like
   - Clear about which files/areas to focus on
   - Explicit about what actions to take (open PRs, commit, just analyze, etc.)
3. **Set the schedule** — Ask when and how often. The user's timezone is Asia/Shanghai. When they say a time (e.g., "every morning at 9am"), assume they mean their local time and convert to UTC for the cron expression. Always confirm the conversion: "9am Asia/Shanghai = Xam UTC." If they want a one-time run (e.g., "once at 3pm", "tomorrow morning", "remind me to check X later"), use `run_once_at` instead of `cron_expression` — same timezone conversion applies. **First re-check the current time with `date -u` via Bash** (the reference time above may be stale in a long conversation), resolve the relative phrase against that fresh value, and confirm the resulting absolute timestamp with the user.

5. **Validate connections** — Infer what services the agent will need from the user's description. For example, if they say "check Datadog and Slack me errors," the agent needs both Datadog and Slack MCP connectors. Cross-reference with the connectors list above. If any are missing, warn the user and link them to https://claude.ai/customize/connectors to connect first. The default git repo is already set to `https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles`. Ask the user if this is the right repo or if they need a different one.
6. **Review and confirm** — Show the full configuration before creating. Let them adjust.
7. **Create it** — Call `RemoteTrigger` with `action: "create"` and show the result. The response includes the routine ID. Always output a link at the end: `https://claude.ai/code/routines/{ROUTINE_ID}`

### UPDATE a routine:

1. List routines first so they can pick one

### LIST routines:

### RUN NOW:

1. List routines if they haven't specified which one
2. Confirm which routine
3. Execute and confirm
